name: Stripe
description: Sets up Stripe products, one-time prices and webhook endpoints with a restricted key, and reads checkouts, payments, customers and events. Webhook signing secrets go straight into an Azure Key Vault, never into any output. Dry run by default; never moves money.

mode.description: dryrun looks everything up and says what it would do, and changes nothing in Stripe or Key Vault; setup in dryrun only reads, and checks each listed vault is reached through Azure management. apply makes the changes; setup in apply also writes the check secret stripe-plugin-check to each listed vault to confirm it can be written.

keyVaults.description: The Azure Key Vaults a webhook signing secret may be written to, by name, such as payments-vault, or by its address ending in vault.azure.net. The plugin finds each vault in the subscriptions the signed-in Microsoft account can read and writes to it through Azure management. Any other vault is refused. Empty: no webhook secret is written anywhere.

expectedAccount.description: The Stripe account (acct_...) the key must belong to. setup names it and keeps it for this member; copy it here to make it permanent. Every run refuses a key for any other account.

apiKey.description: A Stripe restricted key (rk_test_... or rk_live_...). A secret key (sk_...) is refused. Make it in the Stripe Dashboard under Developers, API keys, Create restricted key, with the permissions the package README lists under "The restricted key's permissions".

microsoft.description: Optional: a Microsoft account with the Contributor or Key Vault Contributor role on the Key Vaults in keyVaults. Used for Azure management only, to write secrets to the Key Vaults in keyVaults.

publishes.summary: A Stripe object was created, updated or removed in apply mode.

fields.name: id
fields.summary: The Stripe id of the object.

fields.name: lookupKey
fields.summary: The lookup key of a product or price; the URL of a webhook endpoint, without its query or fragment.

fields.name: environment
fields.summary: test or live, from the key.

publishes.summary: A command was refused: a secret key, a key for another account, a vault not in keyVaults, or bad arguments; or setup found the key lacks a needed permission, which the reason names.

fields.name: command
fields.summary: The command, such as price ensure, without its arguments.
